subject: Culture
title: Food Diplomacy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Food Diplomacy.

hook.text: Nixon ate Peking duck with Mao in 1972. That meal helped reopen US-China relations.

buildup.text: State dinners are strategic. The menu is a diplomatic signal—chosen to honor, impress, or provoke.

discovery.text: South Korea uses 'gastrodiplomacy'—promoting Korean food abroad to build cultural soft power.

twist.text: Thailand's 'Global Thai' program put Thai restaurants worldwide. Food exports more culture than embassies.

climax.text: A well-chosen meal can open negotiations that speeches cannot. Food disarms before words begin.

punchline.text: The table is the oldest negotiation room.

quiz.question: What is 'gastrodiplomacy'?
options: Using food promotion to build soft power

details.summary: Food diplomacy uses cuisine as a tool of international relations — from state banquets designed to impress foreign leaders to Thailand's 'gastrodiplomacy' program that uses restaurants to build global soft power.
details.whyItMatters: Food diplomacy shows how governments weaponize cuisine for geopolitical advantage. Thailand, South Korea, and Peru have all launched official culinary diplomacy programs to boost national influence.
takeaways: Thailand's Global Thai program subsidized Thai restaurants worldwide
South Korea promoted kimchi and K-food as cultural soft power
State banquet menus are carefully designed diplomatic messages

faq.question: What is gastrodiplomacy?
faq.answer: Gastrodiplomacy uses cuisine to build a nation's international image and influence. Thailand pioneered this with its Global Thai program, subsidizing Thai restaurant openings worldwide to spread Thai culture. South Korea, Japan, Peru, and Taiwan have launched similar programs.

faq.question: How do state banquets serve diplomatic purposes?
faq.answer: State banquet menus are crafted by diplomats, not just chefs. Serving a guest's national cuisine shows respect. Using local specialties asserts cultural pride. Dietary restrictions must be navigated (halal, kosher, vegetarian). Even seating arrangements and table settings send messages.
